summary: This paper reports a fully archived preregistered paired experiment testing a Generate–Verify–Repair (GVR) intervention versus an unconstrained baseline for intent→configuration NetOps translation on a synthetic 240-task bank. Execution artifacts show the run completed as recorded under shared_initial_candidate semantics: a single generated candidate per task was reused across arms, every candidate passed the deterministic verifier, no repairs were applied, and the paired contingency was n11=240 (estimate 0.0, McNemar p=1.00, 95% CI [0.0,0.0]). The manuscript is well documented with extensive artifact manifests, but important procedural and inferential clarifications are needed before finalisation.
critical_issues: A prespecified primary comparison (C vs B: GVR vs schema-constrained baseline) from the preregistration was not executed and the execution artifacts contain no recorded rationale. This is a prespecified deviation that must be explicitly declared and discussed in the manuscript as an unexecuted preregistered analysis with its consequences for interpretation.

The preregistered power/precision plan (targeting a ~10 percentage-point paired reduction with N=240) implicitly assumes ability to observe discordant pairs under independent per-condition generation. The executed design used shared_initial_candidate (one candidate reused across arms), which materially reduces sensitivity to detect paired differences; the manuscript must explicitly reconcile the preregistered power calculation with the shared-generation semantics and state that the original power assumptions do not apply to the archived execution.

Although the authors state the shared_initial_candidate semantics caused the null result, the manuscript must (a) clearly enumerate which preregistered analyses were executed vs unexecuted, (b) formally report that multiplicity correction was prespecified but not applied because only one comparison was executed, and (c) state how this affects inferential claims. These clarifications must be placed in Methods/Preregistration and repeated in Abstract/Conclusions for readers.

The manuscript currently leans heavily on provenance and artifact inventories. It must ensure the main narrative reads as a concise scientific conference paper (clear prior-work positioning, methods, quantitative results, interpretation, and limitations) rather than primarily as an artifact-reporting ledger. Replace or condense excessive provenance bookkeeping in main text, keeping artifact references to supplementary/archival paths (artifacts themselves are sufficient for reproducibility).
required_revisions: Add an explicit, prominent preregistration-fidelity disclosure section that (i) lists the two prespecified primary comparisons, (ii) states which were executed and which were not (C vs A executed; C vs B not executed), and (iii) documents that no recorded rationale for the omitted prespecified comparison exists in the archived execution artifacts (treat omission as a prespecified-deviation disclosure rather than an unexplained omission). Cite the specific execution manifest/artifact paths supporting these facts.

Revise the Power & Sampling discussion to reconcile preregistered power assumptions with the actual shared_initial_candidate execution semantics. Explicitly state that the original power calculation assumed independent per-condition generation (discordance potential) and therefore that the archived design materially reduces the study’s sensitivity; remove or qualify any claims that the confirmatory sample size provided the preregistered power for the executed configuration.

In Methods (Preregistration / Analysis) and Results, explicitly report that Bonferroni multiplicity correction was prespecified for two primary comparisons, explain that only one comparison was executed and therefore the correction was not applied to the reported p-value, and discuss how this deviation affects Type I error control and interpretation of the null result.

Include a concise summary (one table or paragraph) within the five-page limit that enumerates all prespecified planned outputs and indicates their execution status and artifact paths (executed / not executed). This must be drawn from the archived manifests (e.g., execution/raw_results.jsonl, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, deterministic_reconciliation.json).

Rework the main text to reduce provenance-heavy prose and present conventional scholarly exposition: a focused Related Work paragraph tying the experiment to nearest prior studies, a compact Methods narrative (with artifact pointers), Results that state numeric outcomes plainly, and a Discussion that emphasizes limitations and implications rather than artifact bookkeeping. Keep detailed provenance references, hashes, and manifest paths but move them to compact paragraphs or an explicitly labeled reproducibility subsection so the paper reads as a conference paper rather than an artifact ledger.
optional_revisions: Summarize (briefly) the conservative sensitivity analyses already archived (e.g., 'failure-as-violation' sensitivity, cluster-stratified checks) in the Results and indicate their artifact paths; the text says these do not change the primary outcome, but a short reported count/table would help readers.

Include a short representative prompt excerpt (or concise sanitized prompt template) in the Methods or Disclosure (the master_prompt path and SHA are supplied; a brief excerpt helps reproducibility and readability).

If space permits, add a one-row summary in Results reporting cluster-level acceptance rates (artifact shows all clusters at 100%) to support the interpretation that the generator+prompt+task distribution produced verifier-compliant outputs across clusters.
